threads.text: Whether to release a public beta of the software tool.

introduced.excerpt: Two labs have used private builds and want us to release a public beta.

latest.excerpt: I am leaning toward releasing an openly downloadable “workshop preview” with a fixed end date, office hours, and no compatibility promise, then deciding on the public beta after we review installation failures and the maintainer returns.

evidence.excerpt: The decision depends on what you want the beta to learn and which failures would be informative rather than merely predictable.
The maintainers' concern still matters because public access changes the volume and variety of support.
Priya expects real use to reveal the right abstractions; the maintainer expects early users to absorb migration and support costs.
One compromise is to use the workshop as an announced hands-on preview and schedule the public beta after the maintainer returns.

threads.text: Whether researchers should be allowed to cite the tool in papers.

introduced.excerpt: Also, the two labs want to cite the tool in papers this year.

latest.excerpt: Citation is the unresolved commitment because it can turn a temporary preview into a durable scholarly object.

evidence.excerpt: The publication and grant benefits are real organizational incentives; they should be named openly rather than translated into an argument that users necessarily need the current interface now.
You could provide a citable project description without presenting the preview interface as stable, but researchers may still cite the software version they used.
